answer: Saffron-seeded identity queues: each new identity must wait through a public queue whose tail position is a hash-graded terrace, so spawning N clones splits one slot into N slower, lower-priority positions. An ember counter decays per identity per epoch; clones exhaust it and fall to the back. Per-clone cost: delayed access plus forfeited queue credits redeemable only after one slot matures, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
